Subject: Request: sizing input for dedicated pool (TL;DR session durations)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Silverline AI is excited about the responsiveness we saw. We're starting procurement and need a concise sizing input from Redwood so our infra team can map budget to expected GPU footprint. High level we need guidance on how session duration (user sessions that keep a KV cache warm) changes fleet sizing vs spike concurrency.

Quick context:
- We have a conversational product used by enterprise customers; sessions are typically 4–12 interactions long.
- 60% of sessions are short (<= 30s active time), 30% medium (30s–3min), 10% long (3–20min).
- Average prompt size: 120 tokens. Average model response: 250 tokens. We plan to use streaming.
- Expected peak concurrent users (QPS-oriented): 1,800 concurrent active sessions during business hours; baseline 300 off-peak.

Can you confirm:
1) How many rtx-like GPUs (or equivalent pool) we should reserve to keep p99 latency under 400ms for streaming responses given a session-aware caching strategy?
2) How much capacity savings do you typically see when prefix/KV caching is effective for multi-turns (e.g., 4–8 exchanges)?
3) Any recommended autoscale/burst settings (burst buffer size, cold-start guardrails)?

I'll attach sample anonymized session logs and a template we filled with top-line numbers. Procurement will need the sizing sheet and a short note to include in the contract.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Silverline AI
Attachments: silverline_session_logs.zip (zip), session-sizing-form.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: sizing input for dedicated pool (TL;DR session durations)

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and the logs, they help a lot. I've looped in Dev (runtime) and Marissa (capacity planning).

High-level answers up front:
1) Ballpark GPU pool: for the numbers you gave (1,800 peak concurrent sessions, streaming, avg 250-token responses), we estimate 18–24 high-memory GPUs (A100- or H100-equivalent) for a non-oversubscribed pool with p99 <= 400ms under target batching and a KV cache retention policy tuned to session length. If you accept moderate (2x) oversubscription you can shrink this to ~12–14 GPUs, but that increases queueing risk during sustained peaks.

2) KV cache impact: when sessions are multi-turn (4–8 turns) and caching is reused, we typically see 25–40% token compute savings vs cold starts — this translates to ~20–30% fewer GPUs needed in many workloads. The exact savings depend on prefix length and model architecture.

3) Autoscale/burst recommendations:
- Set burst capacity for short spikes equal to ~20% of baseline pool with a fast ramp (30–60s) to avoid immediate drops.
- Cold-start guardrail: keep a small warm buffer of 8–10 GPUs (or 10–15% of reserved pool) for sub-second cold-starts.
- Queueing policy: favor latency SLOs for high-value endpoints; allow longer throughput routes to be queued with an upper limit.

I've completed the attached session-sizing-form.xlsx with our baseline numbers and assumptions. Dev/Marissa — please review the assumptions in the sheet and the sample logs Elena sent, then add any kernel/kernel-selection or quantization recommendations to the sizing notes. Marissa, we should also produce a short one-paragraph note for procurement on SLA implications for reserved capacity + burst.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: session-sizing-form.xlsx
